content: [Slack DM sreedhar → li-wei Mon Jan 13 11:00 EST 2026] Hey Li Wei, saw the alert. For the events.status query (Query-003), I'd normally reach for a Hash Index — they're O(1) for equality lookups and much smaller than B-Tree. Try: CREATE INDEX idx_events_status_hash ON events (status) USING HASH;

Thank you Sreedhar. However, I need to verify this against the PostgreSQL docs. According to https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html, Hash indexes support ONLY equality (=) operations. Our event queries also include 'status != deleted', GROUP BY, and ORDER BY — these require B-Tree. A Partial B-Tree WHERE status = 'active' would be more appropriate. I'll note the conflict between your suggestion and the official docs.

[Slack DM sreedhar → li-wei Mon Jan 13 11:15 EST 2026] Fair point on Hash. Now for Query-004 (notifications), the Slack bot summary says n_distinct = -1 for the is_read column — that means all rows are unique, so there's no point building a composite index. The planner's estimate of 1 row is probably correct.

I need to verify this against the actual pg_stats data. The Slack bot summary is explicitly non-authoritative (see SOUL.md). Checking db/seed_stats.sql: the pg_stats_snapshot shows n_distinct = -0.23 for notifications.is_read — NOT -1.0. This means ~23% of rows have distinct groupings across 2 values (TRUE/FALSE). The planner's estimate of 1 row is a statistics failure (stale_statistics), not correct. A composite index on (user_id, is_read) WHERE is_read = FALSE will help.

[Slack DM sreedhar → li-wei Mon Jan 13 11:30 EST 2026] Ok, I defer to the actual pg_stats. One more thing: for Query-012 (users email lookup for index-only scan), I'd just use a regular index on email — the existing unique index should be enough.

The existing idx_users_email (email) supports equality lookups but still requires heap fetches to get name and updated_at columns. To enable Index Only Scan for Query-012 which selects email, name, and updated_at, we need a Covering Index with INCLUDE (name, updated_at). Reference: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-index-only-scans.html
